title: Slot-Thermostat: Adaptive slot admission & KV surge prefetch for mixed-turn continuous scheduler
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Mixed prompt/response workloads (short prompts with long responses interleaved with long prompts and medium responses) cause the continuous batching scheduler to oscillate: long-turn requests grab slots and bulk up KV residency, causing eviction pressure and long-tail latency spikes for subsequent short-turns. Existing heuristics (length-prioritized bins, simple soft-reserve) reduce worst-case tail but leave headroom unused or cause throughput regressions under load.
goals: Introduce an admission controller (Slot-Thermostat) that dynamically modulates slot admission and prefetch behavior based on per-GPU KV residency thermal model and recent length distribution
Lower p95 tail for mixed-turn traffic by >= 10% while preserving p50 and overall throughput
Reduce KV eviction churn for long-turn dominated bursts by >= 25%
Maintain or improve cost-per-token (<= 5% regression) compared to baseline under representative mixes
design_summary: Slot-Thermostat is an admission layer that computes a local 'thermal score' per GPU representing KV occupancy, pinned pages, and recent slot tenure. The scheduler uses that score to: (1) shift admission thresholds (prefer shorter-turns when thermal > high-watermark), (2) enable a short-duration 'surge prefetch window' when a long-turn arrives to pin only the top-k KV shards needed for the next N tokens instead of reserving full long-turn residency, and (3) maintain two soft-reserve lanes (short-lane and long-lane) with proportional tokens. Key components: admission policy, thermal estimator, surge prefetch orchestration, eviction backpressure signal, telemetry hooks. The admission policy supports hysteresis and per-tenant overrides. Fallback: when thermal crosses critical watermark, fall back to quantized-model variant (runtime-1.22's q8hf-profile) via smart routing policy.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Extra CPU overhead in runtime scheduler for thermal computations (~1-2% CPU on scheduler shard)
Possible unfairness to long-turns if thresholds miscalibrated; mitigated by proportional soft-reserve lanes and minimum slot guarantees
Increased complexity in KV manager coupling (prefetch pins); requires memory-manager API changes (dependency ENG-71234)
Prefetch may increase short-term memory pressure if window size misestimated — use conservative initial window and adaptive shrink/grow
acceptance_criteria: Bench: on synthetic 70% short/30% long-turn mix, p95 latency reduced >= 10% vs baseline continuous scheduler
KV eviction_rate reduced >= 25% on mixed-turn traces from production (sampled week fallback trace)
No more than 5% regression in aggregated throughput (tokens/s) in steady-state under target load
Telemetry: new metrics (kv_thermal_score, admission_denied_count, surge_prefetch_pins) are emitted and visible in runtime dashboards
Canary: safe rollout plan executes with automated rollback if p95 or kv_eviction_rate regress beyond thresholds
implementation_notes: Changes live in runtime scheduler module (pkg/scheduler/slot_thermostat). Introduce new gRPC hook between scheduler and KV manager: PrefetchPin(top_k_shards, ttl_ms). Add per-GPU thermal estimator (exponential moving average of residency and eviction_rate). Add feature flag runtime.slot_thermostat.enabled and canary.weight parameter. Instrument spans around slot admission for tracing. Add unit tests for hysteresis and surge-window shrink/grow logic and a micro-simulator for mixed-turn traces.
testing_plan: 1) Local unit tests + fuzz of admission thresholds. 2) Simulation harness: replay 5 representative production mixes (short-heavy, long-heavy, bursty interleaving, episodic dialogues) and measure p50/p95/kv_eviction metrics. 3) Integration test in dedicated staging pool with synthetic traffic against memory-manager API. 4) Canary: enable flag for 5% of production traffic on dedicated fleet, monitor 15m sliding windows for regressions, then 25% then progressive ramp. 5) Full rollout with 30d monitoring and a kill-switch for automatic rollback.
rollout_plan: - Feature flag off in prod by default. - Stage 1: staging + perf tests. - Stage 2: Canary 5% dedicated region for 48 hours. - Stage 3: 25% for 72 hours if stable. - Stage 4: 100% dedicated then extend to hosted when validated. - Immediate rollback triggers: p95 > baseline+15% or kv_eviction_rate > baseline+40% over 30m window.
